syllabus_version.title: CBSE Curriculum for the Academic Year 2026-27

topics.title: The Wit that Won Hearts: the story
topics.ncert_sections: The Wit that Won Hearts: Let us read, Let us discuss, Let us think and reflect

concepts.learning_objective: Students will recall the setting of the story, the court of Krishnadeva Raya and Tenali Ramakrishna's place in it.
Students will explain how Tenali Rama used wit to make the king see his mistake and end the quarrel.

topics.title: The Wit that Won Hearts: words and expressions
topics.ncert_sections: The Wit that Won Hearts: Let us learn I-III

concepts.learning_objective: Students will interpret the meanings of words and expressions from the story in context.
Students will identify closed, hyphenated and open compound words and form new ones.
Students will choose suitable sound words to complete sentences.

topics.title: Conditional sentences (if clauses)
topics.ncert_sections: The Wit that Won Hearts: Let us learn IV-VI

concepts.learning_objective: Students will identify the subordinate (if) clause and the main clause in a sentence.
Students will distinguish possible, hypothetical and past unreal conditions and use the right verb forms.

topics.title: A Concrete Example: the poem
topics.ncert_sections: A Concrete Example: Let us read, Let us discuss, Let us think and reflect

concepts.learning_objective: Students will understand what the poem says about Mrs. Jones and her garden of stones.
Students will identify refrain, rhyme scheme, situational irony and pun in the poem.

topics.title: A Concrete Example: vocabulary
topics.ncert_sections: A Concrete Example: Let us learn I-III

concepts.learning_objective: Students will choose the word that best replaces a word from the poem in context.
Students will distinguish implement, tool, equipment, appliance and gadget.
Students will form new words by replacing the first letter of a given word.

topics.title: Wisdom Paves the Way: the play
topics.ncert_sections: Wisdom Paves the Way: Scene I, Scene II, Let us discuss, Let us think and reflect

concepts.learning_objective: Students will explain how each young man deduced a fact about the camel from its tracks and surroundings.
Students will analyse the merchant's and the King's reactions and the play's message about wisdom.

topics.title: Wisdom Paves the Way: language
topics.ncert_sections: Wisdom Paves the Way: Let us learn I-VI

concepts.learning_objective: Students will form nouns from verbs used in the play.
Students will understand expressions such as 'taken aback' and 'more than meets the eye'.
Students will identify the function of modal verbs and use them correctly.

topics.title: A Tale of Valour: the Battle of Badgam
topics.ncert_sections: A Tale of Valour (main text, the events of 3 November 1947)

concepts.learning_objective: Recall and sequence the events that led to and made up the Battle of Badgam.
Interpret how Major Somnath Sharma's actions and words show leadership and duty.

topics.title: A Tale of Valour: life, legacy and language
topics.ncert_sections: A Tale of Valour (early life, Param Vir Chakra, Let us learn)

concepts.learning_objective: Recall facts about Major Somnath Sharma's early life, honours and legacy.
Use the chapter's vocabulary, noun/verb spelling pairs and collective nouns for armed forces correctly.
Choose verbs that agree with their subjects, including collective nouns.

topics.title: Somebody's Mother: story and theme
topics.ncert_sections: Somebody's Mother (poem, Let us discuss, Let us think and reflect)

concepts.learning_objective: Recall what happens in the poem and in what order.
Analyse the poem's message of empathy and the boy's motive for helping.

topics.title: Somebody's Mother: poetic devices and vocabulary
topics.ncert_sections: Somebody's Mother (poetic devices, Let us learn)

concepts.learning_objective: Identify simile, contrast and the rhyme scheme in the poem.
Use the 'hand' idioms and the conjunction 'lest' correctly.

topics.title: Verghese Kurien - I Too Had A Dream: the letter and its values
topics.ncert_sections: Verghese Kurien - I Too Had A Dream (letter to his grandson)

concepts.learning_objective: Recall the content and purpose of Dr Kurien's letter to Siddharth.
Evaluate the values of integrity, effort and service the letter promotes.

topics.title: Verghese Kurien - I Too Had A Dream: language study
topics.ncert_sections: Verghese Kurien - I Too Had A Dream (Let us discuss, Let us learn, Let us speak)

concepts.learning_objective: Distinguish facts from opinions in sentences from the letter.
Use the en dash, the em dash and its/it's, your/you're, their/they're correctly.
Match words from the letter with synonyms and apply noun/verb stress patterns.

topics.title: The Case of the Fifth Word: the story and its characters
topics.ncert_sections: The Case of the Fifth Word, Part I

concepts.learning_objective: Describe Leroy (Encyclopedia) Brown's traits and his role in solving his father's cases.
Recall the facts of the Diamond Mart hold-up and the suspicion against Nolan and Davenport.

topics.title: The Case of the Fifth Word: the coded message
topics.ncert_sections: The Case of the Fifth Word, Part II

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how Nolan's four-word code stood for days of the week and pointed to the fir tree.
Distinguish statements of fact from statements of opinion in the story.

topics.title: The Case of the Fifth Word: language and grammar
topics.ncert_sections: The Case of the Fifth Word, Let us learn

concepts.learning_objective: Use the phrasal verbs from the story according to their meanings.
Identify homophone pairs and correct spoonerisms.
Change Wh- and Yes/No questions from direct into reported speech.

topics.title: The Magic Brush of Dreams: story, theme and symbols
topics.ncert_sections: The Magic Brush of Dreams (poem)

concepts.learning_objective: Recall the events of the poem and contrast Gopi's and the Zamindar's aims.
Interpret the symbols and the changing tone of the poem.

topics.title: The Magic Brush of Dreams: poetic form and language
topics.ncert_sections: The Magic Brush of Dreams, Let us learn and Let us speak

concepts.learning_objective: Identify the poem's genre, rhyme scheme and use of repetition.
Match interjections to emotions and the verb 'draw' to its meanings in context.

topics.title: Spectacular Wonders: India's natural phenomena
topics.ncert_sections: Spectacular Wonders

concepts.learning_objective: Recall the location and unique feature of each natural wonder described.
Explain the scientific causes behind the phenomena described.

topics.title: Spectacular Wonders: vocabulary and grammar
topics.ncert_sections: Spectacular Wonders, Let us learn

concepts.learning_objective: Use binomials and synonyms of words from the text correctly.
Distinguish participles used as adjectives from gerunds used as nouns.

topics.title: The Cherry Tree, Part I: Planting the Seed

concepts.learning_objective: Describe Rakesh's life with his grandfather in the Himalayan foothills near Mussoorie.
Explain how and why Rakesh planted the cherry seed on Grandfather's advice.
Interpret Rakesh's care for the young cherry tree and its first setbacks.

topics.title: The Cherry Tree, Part II: The Tree Grows and Blossoms

concepts.learning_objective: Trace how the cherry tree survives damage and grows alongside Rakesh.
Identify the creatures that visit the tree and what Rakesh's response shows about him.
Evaluate what the story says about the bond between people and the nature they nurture.

topics.title: The Cherry Tree: Vocabulary and Grammar

concepts.learning_objective: Use the meanings, synonyms and antonyms of words from the story.
Distinguish and use the Simple Past, Past Progressive and Past Perfect tenses.
Identify the use of common punctuation marks such as the colon and semicolon.

topics.title: Harvest Hymn: Meaning, Structure and Poetic Devices

concepts.learning_objective: Explain whom the farmers praise in the hymn and why they offer thanks.
Identify alliteration, personification and metaphor in lines of the poem.
Analyse why the poem is a hymn sung in the voices of men, women and all.

topics.title: Harvest Hymn: Archaic Words and Vocabulary

concepts.learning_objective: Give the modern meanings of archaic words such as thou, thee, thy, thine and art.
Infer the meanings of words such as munificent, succour, counsel and ineffable.

topics.title: Waiting for the Rain: Velu and the Drought

concepts.learning_objective: Describe Velu's life as a farmer and his response to the failed rains.
Interpret the old woman's advice that the land, like people, needs rest.
Relate the story's idea of resting land to the practice of fallowing.

topics.title: Waiting for the Rain: Vocabulary and Grammar

concepts.learning_objective: Identify and use homophones such as weather and whether, piece and peace.
Distinguish and use the Simple Present, Present Progressive and Present Perfect tenses.
Infer the meanings of words such as forlorn, dejected and muttered from context.

topics.title: Feathered Friend: Claribel aboard the space station
topics.ncert_sections: Feathered Friend, Part I

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how Claribel came to the space station and adapted to weightlessness.
Interpret the narrator's description of construction work and life in free fall.

topics.title: Feathered Friend: the warning that saved the crew
topics.ncert_sections: Feathered Friend, Part II

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how Claribel's collapse revealed the danger in the station's air.
Identify why the alarm failed and interpret the humour of the ending.

topics.title: Feathered Friend: merged words and future time
topics.ncert_sections: Feathered Friend, Let us learn

concepts.learning_objective: Form merged words and state their source words.
Choose the verb form that expresses future time correctly in context.

topics.title: Magnifying Glass: theme, imagery and form
topics.ncert_sections: Magnifying Glass (poem)

concepts.learning_objective: Interpret how the poem shows ordinary things becoming wonderful under a lens.
Identify the poem's devices, stanza form and rhyme scheme.

topics.title: Magnifying Glass: collective nouns, idioms and suffix -ish
topics.ncert_sections: Magnifying Glass, Let us learn

concepts.learning_objective: Match collective nouns with the groups they name.
Use idioms with 'eye' correctly in context.
Form adjectives by adding the suffix -ish to suitable nouns.

topics.title: Bibha Chowdhuri: a pioneer of physics
topics.ncert_sections: Bibha Chowdhuri, Let us read (opening to Breaking Boundaries)

concepts.learning_objective: Recall the main events of Bibha Chowdhuri's career in order.
Explain the importance of Bibha Chowdhuri's research on cosmic rays.

topics.title: Bibha Chowdhuri: legacy and women in Indian science
topics.ncert_sections: Bibha Chowdhuri, The Legacy and From Shadows to the Stars

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how Bibha Chowdhuri's work was finally honoured.
Evaluate how the text links her struggle to women scientists today.

topics.title: Bibha Chowdhuri: suffixes, clipping and passive voice
topics.ncert_sections: Bibha Chowdhuri, Let us learn

concepts.learning_objective: Form nouns by adding the suffixes -ship, -ment and -hood.
Identify back, front and middle clipping in shortened words.
Use the passive voice correctly and explain when it is preferred.
